# Dictionary

An intelligent multi-modal dictionary: English definitions, IPA, etymology, **personal-name meanings in ten languages and scripts**,
grounded AI answers (agentic pipeline + RAG), on-device OCR, flashcards, and a Groq ⇄ Gemini chatbot (LexiBot).

* **Front end** — static multi-page site (no framework), generated by `scripts/build.mjs`. Deploys to Vercel.
* **Back end (optional)** — FastAPI gateway, agent pipeline, hybrid retrieval, vision service, Redis, Postgres, Qdrant in Docker.

```
dictionary/
├─ site.config.mjs        ← name, author, local-business schema, repo URL (edit this)
├─ scripts/               ← build.mjs (pages, SEO, sitemap…), verify.mjs (audit), serve.mjs, make-assets.py
├─ src/assets/            ← css/, js/, img/ (architecture diagram)
├─ public/                ← favicons, manifest, social share images
├─ backend/               ← FastAPI app, RAG, agents, tests, Dockerfile
├─ vision/                ← OCR + object-classification microservice
├─ deploy/                ← nginx.conf, k8s/api.yaml
├─ db/init.sql            ← Postgres schema
├─ docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile.web, vercel.json, .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

## 1. Run it on your computer

```bash
npm install          # installs esbuild (used only to minify)
npm run build        # → dist/
npm run verify       # audits titles, meta, canonicals, h1, alt text, links, JSON-LD, sitemap, source maps
npm run dev          # build + serve on http://localhost:3000 (mimics Vercel clean URLs and the 404 page)
```

Backend tests (no installs needed, Python 3.10+):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=backend python3 -m unittest discover -s backend/tests -v
```

Full stack (needs Docker):

```bash
cp .env.example backend/.env       # then add GROQ_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY (free tiers) and generate API_KEYS
export POSTGRES_PASSWORD='choose-a-long-random-password'
docker compose up --build          # site on http://localhost:3000, API proxied at /api
```

## 2. Put it on GitHub — from your phone with Termux

You can do the whole thing from Android. Install **Termux from F-Droid** (the Play Store build is outdated).

**A. One-time setup**

```bash
pkg update -y && pkg upgrade -y
pkg install -y git nodejs openssh unzip
termux-setup-storage                 # allow storage access, tap "Allow"
git config --global user.name  "Nikhil Chary Sriramoju"
git config --global user.email "sriramojunikhil66@gmail.com"
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
```

**B. Get the project into Termux.** Put `dictionary.zip` in your phone's Downloads folder, then:

```bash
cd ~
unzip ~/storage/downloads/dictionary.zip
cd dictionary
```

**C. Create the empty repo on GitHub.** In your phone browser: github.com → **+** → **New repository** → name it `dictionary` →
leave README, .gitignore and licence **unticked** (they already exist) → **Create repository**.

**D. Make a login token** (GitHub no longer accepts your password for git).
github.com → profile photo → **Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens → Generate new token**.
Repository access: **Only select repositories → dictionary**. Permissions: **Contents: Read and write**. Copy the token (starts with `github_pat_`).

**E. Push**

```bash
git init -b main
git add .
git status                           # make sure .env and node_modules are NOT listed
git commit -m "Initial commit: Dictionary"
git remote add origin https://github.com/Nikhil-creat/dictionary.git
git push -u origin main
```

When it asks **Username** type `Nikhil-creat`; when it asks **Password** paste the token (nothing shows as you paste — that's normal).
To avoid pasting it again: `git config --global credential.helper store` *before* the push.

**Optional: SSH key instead of a token**

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "sriramojunikhil66@gmail.com"
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub            # copy it → GitHub → Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:Nikhil-creat/dictionary.git
ssh -T git@github.com && git push -u origin main
```

**F. Later changes**

```bash
git add . && git commit -m "describe the change" && git push
```

Vercel redeploys automatically on every push. The **ci** workflow also runs (Actions tab): site build + audit, backend
tests, Trivy scan and a Lighthouse check (the Lighthouse step is untested until it runs on GitHub — if it fails, open the
run and read the report).

Never commit secrets: `.env` is git-ignored. If you ever paste a token into a file by mistake, delete the token on GitHub and make a new one.

### Optional: also host it free on GitHub Pages

The site uses root-absolute paths, so it must be served from the root of a domain. A project repo (`dictionary`) would be served at
`/dictionary/` and break. Use a **user-site repo** instead: create an empty repo named exactly `Nikhil-creat.github.io`, then:

```bash
git remote add pages https://github.com/Nikhil-creat/Nikhil-creat.github.io.git
git push -u pages main
```

On GitHub: that repo → **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**. The `pages` workflow builds the site with
`SITE_URL=https://nikhil-creat.github.io` and deploys it. After that, push to both: `git push origin main && git push pages main`.
GitHub Pages cannot send the security headers in `vercel.json` (CSP, HSTS); Vercel remains the recommended production host.

## GitHub repo description, topics and SEO keywords

**About → Description** (paste into the gear icon beside "About" on the repo page):

> Dictionary: an intelligent multi-modal dictionary with word definitions, etymology and name meanings in 10 languages. Four-agent AI pipeline, hybrid RAG, on-device OCR and a Groq + Gemini chatbot. FastAPI, Docker, Vercel.

**Website:** your Vercel URL.  **Topics** (add all):
`dictionary` `multilingual` `name-meanings` `etymology` `agentic-ai` `rag` `retrieval-augmented-generation` `llm` `groq` `gemini` `ocr` `computer-vision` `fastapi` `docker` `vercel` `threejs` `javascript` `python` `nlp` `portfolio`

**Site keywords** live in `site.config.mjs` (`keywords`) and are rendered on every page. Search engines mostly ignore the keywords tag,
so the titles, descriptions, headings and structured data matter more; the keywords are a convenience for other tools.

## 3. Deploy the front end on Vercel

1. vercel.com → **Add New… → Project** → **Import** your `dictionary` repo.
2. **Framework Preset: Other.** Build command, output directory (`dist`) and headers come from `vercel.json` — leave the defaults.
3. Click **Deploy**. Vercel exposes your production domain at build time, so canonical URLs, the sitemap and share images use it
   automatically.
4. Open the site and check `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt`, a missing URL (custom 404) and a name page such as `/names/nikhil`.

## 4. Custom domain

1. Buy a domain (any registrar).
2. Vercel → your project → **Settings → Domains → Add** `yourdomain.com` (and `www.yourdomain.com`).
3. Add the DNS records Vercel displays at your registrar (use the values shown in the dashboard — they can differ per project).
   Wait for the certificate to be issued (usually minutes).
4. **Settings → Environment Variables** → add `SITE_URL` = `https://yourdomain.com` (Production) → **Deployments → Redeploy**.
   This rewrites every canonical tag, Open Graph URL, JSON-LD URL, the sitemap and `llms.txt`.
5. Choose which hostname is primary (Domains page) and redirect the other to it.
6. Google Search Console → add the property → submit `https://yourdomain.com/sitemap.xml`.

## 5. Backend hosting (optional)

Vercel serves the static site; it does not run Docker Compose. Run the backend on any container host (a VPS with Docker, Render,
Fly.io, Railway, a Kubernetes cluster — `deploy/k8s/api.yaml` is a starting point), then:

* set `CORS_ORIGINS=https://yourdomain.com` on the API;
* set `API_BASE=https://api.yourdomain.com` in Vercel and redeploy — the lookup page then sends AI calls to your server
  (keys stay server-side) instead of asking visitors for their own Groq/Gemini keys.

## Things to personalise

* `site.config.mjs` — `business` drives the LocalBusiness (ProfessionalService) schema on the home and About pages. It currently has
  city/region/country only. **If you want Google to treat it as a local business, add a real street address, phone number and opening
  hours** (and only publish details you actually want public).
* About page (`scripts/pages.mjs`) — credentials and projects. Add new certificates to the `issuers` list and update the counts.
* Email address on the About page/footer is public; change `site.config.mjs` if you prefer a different one.
* Names — add entries to `src/assets/js/names-data.js`, then run
  `node -e "import('./src/assets/js/names-data.js').then(m=>require('fs').writeFileSync('backend/data/names.json',JSON.stringify(Object.values(m.NAMES),null,1)))"`
  so the backend corpus matches. Every name gets its own page, sitemap entry and `llms.txt` line automatically.

## What was verified, and what was not

Verified here: the static build and the launch-checklist audit (`npm run verify`: unique titles/descriptions, canonical, one `h1`,
alt text, internal links, JSON-LD parses, sitemap matches pages, no source maps); a headless-browser run of all pages at phone width
(no horizontal overflow, no script errors), the lookup flows with mocked APIs (names, words, graph, flashcards, offline cache,
Groq→Gemini failover with model auto-detection), the custom 404, and 21 backend unit tests (sanitising, RBAC, rate limiter, hybrid
retrieval, LLM failover/breaker, grounding validator, neologism moderation).

Not verified here (no network/Docker/GPU in the build sandbox): the real three.js globe and its shaders (the logic ran against a stand-in
module), in-browser OCR/object recognition (CDN models), the FastAPI app under uvicorn, the vision service, the Docker images, Qdrant and
Redis integrations, Kubernetes manifests, and esbuild minification. Run the checklist in section 1 and `docker compose up --build`, and
treat any failure there as a bug to report.

## Known limitations (also stated on the site's /security page)

* AI answers are only as good as the retrieval corpus; the seed corpus is small. Anything the validator cannot ground is labelled unverified.
* Dense retrieval defaults to a character n-gram hashing embedder (no downloads). For stronger cross-lingual alignment, plug a multilingual
  sentence-transformer into `HybridStore(embedder=...)`.
* The agent pipeline is a plain-Python state machine, not LangGraph; OCR uses Tesseract (LSTM), not CRAFT/TrOCR; objects use EfficientNet-B0.
* Neologisms are held in memory; `db/init.sql` is the schema for a Postgres-backed repository you can add next.
* Voter identity for neologism upvotes is role + IP — fine for a demo, replace with real accounts before relying on it.

## Next steps

Real user accounts (JWT) backed by Postgres, a Wiktionary/WordNet ingestion job into the vector store, a multilingual embedder, and
